{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"a0a8806f-08e3-4358-ae84-15c674a16782\",\"title\":\"Architecture & Delivery Plan — MCP-2: Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform\",\"content\":\"# Architecture & Delivery Plan\\n\\nBacklog issue: [MCP-2 — Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform>)\\n\\n## Purpose\\n\\nDefine a phased architecture that turns the current McpFn server/runtime and regression foundation into:\\n\\n* a concise production server SDK;\\n* a production client SDK;\\n* an MCP-specific authorization lifecycle that composes generic OAuth/AuthFn primitives;\\n* one target/session/diagnostic engine shared by tests, CLI, and a future inspector;\\n* release and migration evidence that names exactly what was verified.\\n\\nThis document is a delivery plan, not an instruction to implement all phases atomically.\\n\\n## Baseline architecture found in the repository\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/core`\\n\\nCurrent responsibilities:\\n\\n* wraps the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` server;\\n* creates a fresh official SDK server for a transport connection;\\n* supports official in-memory, stdio, and Streamable HTTP/Web Standard transports;\\n* registers tools, resources, resource templates, prompts, completions, subscriptions, and experimental tasks;\\n* exposes client-mediated sampling, elicitation, roots, notifications, and task APIs to handlers;\\n* validates input and structured output with Ajv;\\n* supports request-derived context and per-request tool visibility;\\n* validates MCP Apps resources, CSP, permissions, and tool-resource metadata;\\n* creates canonical manifests and structural compatibility diffs;\\n* preserves stable domain error codes where possible.\\n\\nArchitectural constraint: retain the official MCP SDK as the sole protocol and transport lifecycle implementation.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/auth`\\n\\nCurrent responsibilities:\\n\\n* computes the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata URL;\\n* serves protected-resource metadata;\\n* parses bearer credentials;\\n* calls an application-supplied token verifier;\\n* enforces expiry, exact resource binding, and required scopes;\\n* forwards trusted `AuthInfo` to the MCP server;\\n* adds enterprise-managed authorization discovery metadata.\\n\\nArchitectural constraint: this is currently resource-server middleware. It must remain usable independently even if McpFn later adds client authorization orchestration.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/testing`\\n\\nCurrent responsibilities:\\n\\n* connects an official client to an McpFn server through an in-memory pair;\\n* lists and invokes capabilities;\\n* compares live inventories with manifests;\\n* runs serial tool-oriented semantic scenarios;\\n* executes API-key and OAuth credential matrices through target/provider contracts;\\n* serves a deterministic mock authorization server;\\n* runs a Playwright authorization-code/PKCE/refresh/revoke flow;\\n* compares manifests with generic host capability profiles;\\n* shells to a pinned official conformance runner.\\n\\nArchitectural constraint: preserve deterministic in-memory coverage, but remove its status as the only first-class target.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/cli`\\n\\nCurrent responsibilities:\\n\\n* load an McpFn server, registry, manifest, or scenario module;\\n* generate/validate/diff manifests;\\n* run McpFn-native scenarios;\\n* run official conformance against a URL;\\n* return stable process exits.\\n\\nArchitectural constraint: programmatic engine APIs must remain primary; CLI commands should be thin adapters.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/datafn`\\n\\nCurrent responsibilities:\\n\\n* maps explicitly selected DataFn resources to bounded MCP tools;\\n* respects DataFn read/write policy;\\n* fixes projections and filter/sort fields;\\n* bounds list limits;\\n* leaves mutations off unless explicitly enabled;\\n* requires idempotency material for writes;\\n* maps trusted server context into DataFn context.\\n\\nArchitectural constraint: retain deny-by-default adapters as the pattern for future domain integrations.\\n\\n## Target architecture\\n\\n### Layer diagram\\n\\n```\\nApplication policy and domain handlers\\n  |\\n  +-- McpFn server facade --------------------------+\\n  |      |                                           |\\n  |      +-- registry / manifests / compatibility   |\\n  |      +-- trusted context / auth adapter          |\\n  |      +-- official MCP SDK server + transports    |\\n  |                                                  |\\n  +-- McpFn production client facade                 |\\n         |\\n         +-- target + session engine <---------------+---- testing runner\\n         |      |                                     +---- CLI\\n         |      +-- official MCP SDK client           +---- future inspector\\n         |      +-- transport adapters\\n         |      +-- capability and event model\\n         |      +-- structured diagnostics\\n         |\\n         +-- MCP authorization orchestrator\\n                +-- protected-resource discovery\\n                +-- authorization-server discovery\\n                +-- registration/client metadata adapters\\n                +-- browser/native callback adapter\\n                +-- shared OAuth PKCE/state/HTTP/storage\\n                +-- token refresh/revocation\\n```\\n\\nThe key design choice is that tests and the inspector do not own a separate MCP client. They consume the same headless session engine as production clients, with testing-specific clocks, fixtures, assertions, and artifact sinks layered around it.\\n\\n## Proposed package responsibilities\\n\\nPackage naming is a Phase 0 decision. The following separation describes responsibilities, not mandatory final npm names.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/core`\\n\\nKeep low-level, runtime-neutral contracts:\\n\\n* schemas, definitions, result/error envelopes;\\n* registry and current server runtime for compatibility;\\n* manifests, canonicalization, and compatibility diffing;\\n* shared capability/event/diagnostic types that do not force browser or Node dependencies.\\n\\nCompatibility option: keep current server exports in core through 1.0, even if a higher-level server package is added.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/server` or server facade in core\\n\\nProvide the concise application-facing declaration/runtime split:\\n\\n* side-effect-free server declaration;\\n* runtime construction with transports, auth, context, storage, observability, and policy;\\n* framework adapters for Web Standard handlers;\\n* explicit request context derivation;\\n* manifest/test hooks from the same declaration;\\n* compatibility adapters for `McpFnRegistry` and `McpFnServer`.\\n\\nDo not move tenant/workspace/permission/confirmation fields into tool arguments.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/client`\\n\\nNew production package:\\n\\n* official-SDK client lifecycle;\\n* stdio and Streamable HTTP target adapters;\\n* connection sharing and idempotent connect/close;\\n* full pagination for tools/resources/templates/prompts;\\n* tool/resource/prompt/task APIs;\\n* notifications, progress, logging, cancellation, subscriptions, and client-mediated capability handlers;\\n* result normalization that preserves raw protocol payloads;\\n* typed, phase-specific errors;\\n* bounded retry and reconnect rules;\\n* optional authorization orchestrator integration;\\n* event/diagnostic sink used by tests and inspector.\\n\\nLangFn's private client and transport code should be treated as migration evidence and a source of behavioral requirements, not copied wholesale without contract review.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/auth`\\n\\nExpand carefully into shared MCP authorization contracts while preserving resource-server APIs:\\n\\n* current protected-resource handler;\\n* `McpFnAuthorizationProvider` or equivalent strategy contract;\\n* discovery result types and validation;\\n* callback/redirect adapter contract;\\n* client registration strategy contract;\\n* token store abstraction compatible with shared encrypted vaults;\\n* server-side adapter contract that maps an authenticated application session to official MCP `AuthInfo`;\\n* standardized redaction and auth diagnostic codes.\\n\\nKeep Node/browser dependencies behind subpath exports or separate packages so the resource-server middleware remains portable.\\n\\n### AuthFn adapter location\\n\\nEvaluate three placements:\\n\\n1. `@mcpfn/auth/authfn` subpath;\\n2. dedicated `@mcpfn/auth-authfn`;\\n3. an adapter exported from AuthFn.\\n\\nDecision criteria:\\n\\n* dependency direction must not force all McpFn users to install AuthFn;\\n* AuthFn's session/plugin internals should remain AuthFn-owned;\\n* McpFn should receive only trusted subject, scopes, resource IDs, expiry, and client identity required by MCP;\\n* adapter versioning must make compatibility visible.\\n\\nRecommended starting point: a small optional adapter package or subpath with AuthFn as a peer dependency. Revisit ownership with the AuthFn team before stabilizing.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/testing`\\n\\nRefactor around the production target/session engine:\\n\\n* in-memory target adapter for deterministic server tests;\\n* stdio target adapter;\\n* remote Streamable HTTP target adapter;\\n* auth credential and OAuth browser harness adapters;\\n* contract assertions for tools/resources/prompts/tasks/capabilities;\\n* semantic scenarios beyond tool calls;\\n* host/provider interoperability profiles;\\n* official conformance orchestration;\\n* secret-redacted artifact model;\\n* deterministic clocks, ports, cleanup, and expected-failure policy.\\n\\n<issue id=\\\"6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8\\\" href=\\\"https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing\\\">MCP-1</issue> should deliver its external-server target and authenticated conformance work through these contracts.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/cli`\\n\\nAdd thin commands only after programmatic APIs exist:\\n\\n* `connect` or `inspect --headless` for discovery/capability diagnostics;\\n* `test` against in-memory, stdio, or HTTP targets;\\n* `auth diagnose` for discovery/registration/redirect validation without printing credentials;\\n* `record` or `export-scenario` if the same format is consumed by tests and inspector;\\n* existing manifest/diff/conformance behavior retained with migration aliases.\\n\\n### `@mcpfn/inspector` and/or inspector application\\n\\nLater phase:\\n\\n* UI over the headless client/session engine;\\n* no private transport or OAuth implementation;\\n* pluggable secret storage, defaulting to memory-only;\\n* redacted session export;\\n* import/export of the same scenario and diagnostics formats as testing;\\n* optional Super Console embedding through a narrow adapter.\\n\\nSuper Console's existing MCP administration inventory is a related operational surface, not a substitute for this inspector.\\n\\n## Proposed application APIs\\n\\nThese examples are illustrative and must not be treated as final names.\\n\\n### Server declaration\\n\\n```ts\\nconst app = defineMcpFnServer({\\n  info: { name: \\\"orders\\\", version: \\\"1.0.0\\\" },\\n  tools: [listOrders, cancelOrder],\\n  auth: mcpResourceAuth({\\n    resource: \\\"https://api.example.com/mcp\\\",\\n    provider: authFnMcpAdapter({ auth }),\\n    authorize: ({ session, tool }) =>\\n      policy.canInvoke(session.subject, tool.name),\\n  }),\\n});\\n\\nconst server = app.createServer({\\n  observability,\\n  context: ({ auth }) => ({\\n    tenantId: requireTenant(auth),\\n    actorId: auth.clientId,\\n  }),\\n});\\n\\nexport const fetch = server.handler({ transport: \\\"streamable-http\\\" });\\n```\\n\\nProperties:\\n\\n* application policy is explicit;\\n* authenticated tenancy is derived from trusted context;\\n* the tool declaration remains reusable for manifests and tests;\\n* the official SDK remains internal to lifecycle.\\n\\n### Production client\\n\\n```ts\\nconst client = createMcpFnClient({\\n  target: streamableHttpTarget(\\\"https://api.example.com/mcp\\\"),\\n  authorization: oauthAuthorization({\\n    client: clientMetadataDocument(\\\"https://app.example.com/mcp-client.json\\\"),\\n    callback: browserCallback({\\n      redirectUri: \\\"https://app.example.com/oauth/mcp/callback\\\",\\n    }),\\n    storage: encryptedTokenStore(...),\\n  }),\\n  diagnostics: event => audit.safe(event),\\n});\\n\\nawait client.connect();\\nconst tools = await client.tools.listAll();\\nconst result = await client.tools.call(\\\"orders_list\\\", { limit: 20 });\\n```\\n\\nProperties:\\n\\n* one connection owns transport and token lifecycle;\\n* auth can be replaced with API key, pre-issued bearer, no-auth, or enterprise adapter;\\n* raw payload access remains available;\\n* diagnostics identify phases without exposing secrets.\\n\\n### Regression suite\\n\\n```ts\\nconst suite = defineMcpFnSuite({\\n  target: streamableHttpTarget(localServer.url),\\n  authorization: providerShapedOAuthFixture(\\\"chatgpt\\\"),\\n  contract: \\\"./mcp.manifest.json\\\",\\n  scenarios: \\\"./mcp.scenarios.ts\\\",\\n  conformance: { version: \\\"0.1.16\\\", suite: \\\"active\\\" },\\n  artifacts: { directory: \\\".artifacts/mcp\\\", redact: \\\"strict\\\" },\\n});\\n\\nawait suite.run();\\n```\\n\\nProperties:\\n\\n* external servers do not adopt McpFn server types;\\n* in-memory tests use the same suite with a different target;\\n* deterministic fixture and live-provider modes are declared separately.\\n\\n## Core target and session contracts\\n\\n### Target\\n\\nA target describes how to create an official-SDK transport and what environment constraints apply.\\n\\n```ts\\ninterface McpFnTarget {\\n  kind: \\\"in-memory\\\" | \\\"stdio\\\" | \\\"streamable-http\\\" | string;\\n  open(context: McpFnTargetContext): Promise<McpFnTransportHandle>;\\n  describe(): RedactedTargetDescriptor;\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe descriptor must never serialize bearer tokens, authorization codes, PKCE verifiers, client secrets, session IDs, or sensitive query parameters.\\n\\n### Session\\n\\nA session owns:\\n\\n* authorization readiness;\\n* official client creation and initialization;\\n* negotiated protocol version and capabilities;\\n* complete paginated inventories;\\n* request correlation;\\n* subscriptions, notifications, tasks, logging, and progress;\\n* cancellation and close;\\n* refresh/reconnect state;\\n* structured event emission.\\n\\nTesting wraps a session with assertions. The inspector subscribes to its events. Production clients expose typed facades over it.\\n\\n### Diagnostic event\\n\\nMinimum shape:\\n\\n```ts\\ninterface McpFnDiagnosticEvent {\\n  phase:\\n    | \\\"resource-discovery\\\"\\n    | \\\"authorization-server-discovery\\\"\\n    | \\\"client-registration\\\"\\n    | \\\"authorization-request\\\"\\n    | \\\"authorization-callback\\\"\\n    | \\\"token-exchange\\\"\\n    | \\\"token-refresh\\\"\\n    | \\\"transport-connect\\\"\\n    | \\\"mcp-initialize\\\"\\n    | \\\"capability-operation\\\";\\n  outcome: \\\"started\\\" | \\\"succeeded\\\" | \\\"failed\\\";\\n  code?: string;\\n  requestId: string;\\n  at: string;\\n  target: RedactedTargetDescriptor;\\n  details?: RedactedJson;\\n}\\n```\\n\\nRedaction must be enforced at event construction, not left to UI/log consumers.\\n\\n## MCP authorization architecture\\n\\n### Role 3 hosted-server ownership decision\\n\\nMcpFn owns the MCP-specific authorization-server compatibility profile even when identity and token authority are supplied by AuthFn, the application, or an external authorization server. A hosted-server adapter must provide:\\n\\n* protected-resource and authorization-server metadata compatible with the MCP deployment;\\n* pre-registered, Dynamic Client Registration, and Client ID Metadata Document strategies;\\n* normalized request-compatible grant/response/token-auth-method negotiation;\\n* redirect URI validation, including approved web/native/loopback policies;\\n* PKCE, state, issuer, resource-indicator, and MCP-scope enforcement;\\n* phase-accurate MCP/OAuth errors and redacted diagnostics;\\n* a narrow bridge to identity, consent, signing, token issuance, and storage adapters.\\n\\nAuthFn owns user authentication, sessions, tenant/region context, and application consent policy. Its existing social OAuth plugin is not treated as an MCP authorization server. McpFn must not duplicate those AuthFn facilities, and consumers must not keep parallel MCP-specific registration or redirect validators after migration.\\n\\n### State machine\\n\\n 1. **Probe the MCP target.**\\n    * Attempt initialization or an authorization-aware probe according to the official SDK/transport contract.\\n    * Parse a bearer challenge and protected-resource metadata URL when authorization is required.\\n 2. **Discover the protected resource.**\\n    * Fetch RFC 9728 metadata.\\n    * Validate resource identity and authorization-server candidates.\\n    * Cache only within explicit TTL and authority boundaries.\\n 3. **Discover/select the authorization server.**\\n    * Fetch metadata from the selected server.\\n    * Validate issuer, endpoints, supported response/grant types, PKCE, token auth methods, and registration capabilities.\\n    * Preserve raw metadata for redacted diagnostics.\\n 4. **Resolve client registration.**\\n    * Pre-registered client ID;\\n    * Client ID Metadata Document;\\n    * Dynamic Client Registration;\\n    * enterprise-managed adapter.\\n\\n    Each strategy returns a normalized registration record with source, allowed redirects, # Ideation & Product Rationale

Backlog issue: [MCP-2 — Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform>)

## Product thesis

McpFn should be the default way an application adds MCP support, whether the application is exposing capabilities as a server, consuming capabilities as a client, validating an MCP implementation in CI, or diagnosing it interactively.

The value is not another wrapper around the official MCP SDK. The value is a coherent application layer that:

* gives consumers concise client and server APIs;
* makes authentication and authorization interoperability explicit and testable;
* turns agent-facing contracts into reviewable manifests and semantic regressions;
* produces consistent diagnostics across local tests, remote servers, CI, and an inspector;
* lets the official MCP SDK and conformance suite continue owning protocol correctness;
* lets the application continue owning domain semantics, tenancy, permission, approval, and destructive-action policy.

The long-term product should feel similar to AuthFn in adoption effort: declare the application surface, supply runtime dependencies and policy, create a server or client, and use typed APIs. “Similar to AuthFn” describes the developer experience and composition model; it does not mean AuthFn already implements the MCP authorization-server protocol.

## User intent captured in this issue

The desired end state is:

* consumers should do little beyond using McpFn client and server SDKs to add MCP support;
* the same McpFn platform should add regression coverage to a consumer's MCP server;
* a future inspector, comparable in purpose to MCPJam or MCP Inspector, should support deeper development and testing workflows;
* the client, server, test harness, CLI, and inspector should share contracts rather than becoming separate products with subtly different behavior;
* the recent ChatGPT/Skillplane `redirect_uri is not registered for this client` failure should be the kind of interoperability regression McpFn can catch before production.

## Current-state evidence from Superfunctions

The repository was inspected at `next` commit `523c66ae`, together with the McpFn-specific review hardening on the open `dev` port through `origin/codex/mcpfn-next-to-dev` commit `1d90f64b`.

| Surface | What exists now | Product implication |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `@mcpfn/core` | Official-SDK server runtime, registry, tool/resource/template/prompt/task support, MCP Apps contracts, manifests/diffs, request context, stdio and Web Standard Streamable HTTP | Strong server foundation; no production client facade |
| `@mcpfn/auth` | Protected-resource metadata, bearer verification, resource/audience validation, scopes, enterprise-managed authorization marker | Correct resource-server boundary; authorization-code lifecycle is intentionally absent |
| `@mcpfn/testing` | In-memory test client, exact contract assertions, semantic tool scenarios, auth matrices, mock OAuth server, browser PKCE flow, host profiles, official conformance wrapper | Useful foundation, but most coverage is closed-loop or McpFn-native |
| `@mcpfn/cli` | `manifest`, `validate`, `diff`, `test`, `conformance` | CI-oriented; no connect/inspect/auth diagnostic surface |
| `@mcpfn/datafn` | Explicit, deny-by-default tool projection with bounded reads and opt-in idempotent writes | Good example of consumer policy remaining explicit |
| LangFn | McpFn server integration plus a separate official-SDK client, stdio/HTTP transports, pagination, result normalization, error mapping, and connection lifecycle | Concrete proof that a production client SDK is missing |
| MemoryFn and ProbeFn | McpFn registry/server integrations | Server consumers still provide substantial domain/tool mapping |
| Super Console | McpFn-backed administrative server plus an MCP inventory page | Potential host for future operational views, but not an inspector today |
| Release gate | Package typecheck/test/build, browser fixture, official conformance, CLI examples, packing; consumer coverage differs between `next` and the open `dev` port | Evidence must name the exact branch and consumer scope |

The five McpFn packages are at `0.0.1`. Their current documentation describes the runtime as intentionally below product-level inspector/evaluation UIs. This issue proposes changing that product boundary in phases.

## Why the redirect failure was not caught

The current test suite is not negligent; it tests the boundary it was designed to own. The blind spot follows from that boundary and from a self-consistent fixture design.

### 1. The resource-server package cannot validate authorization-server configuration

`@mcpfn/auth` receives a bearer token after authorization has already happened. It can advertise protected-resource metadata and validate token scopes/resource binding, but it never constructs an authorization request and never compares the request's `redirect_uri` with registered client metadata.

A redirect-registration rejection occurs before any token reaches the resource server. No resource-server-only library can catch it without an additional client/authorization interoperability layer.

### 2. The OAuth browser fixture controls both sides

The mock authorization server generates its own issuer, callback URL, client metadata, authorization endpoint, token endpoint, and accepted redirect set. The Playwright test then asks the fixture for those exact values. That proves PKCE, browser approval, code exchange, refresh, and revocation inside the fixture, but it cannot expose configuration drift between independently deployed systems.

The test does not currently model:

* a client deriving a callback from one public origin while registration uses another;
* a native or loopback client choosing a dynamic port;
* multiple registered redirect URIs and selection rules;
* pre-registration versus DCR versus Client ID Metadata Document behavior;
* a host/provider independently interpreting client metadata;
* deployment/configuration propagation or stale registration;
* issuer identification and callback parameters supplied by an external authorization server;
* a production MCP client performing discovery before the browser flow.

### 3. The McpFn test client bypasses network and OAuth

`McpFnTestClient.connect(server)` creates an official in-memory transport pair. It is excellent for deterministic server semantics, but it does not traverse protected-resource discovery, HTTP challenges, authorization-server metadata, redirect/callback handling, token storage, or an authenticated Streamable HTTP connection.

### 4. Host profiles are intentionally generic

Current profiles describe broad capability classes such as tools-only, full-protocol, and MCP Apps. They do not claim named host/provider behavior. That avoids stale claims, but it also means there is no deterministic “ChatGPT-shaped client against this authorization-server policy” regression.

### 5. A green release gate proves the fixture and package scope

The Chromium PKCE test proves the controlled fixture works. Official conformance proves supported protocol scenarios. Neither is a live provider/configuration test. The release gate should keep these proofs, but McpFn needs additional provider-shaped and controlled live-smoke layers with clearly different claims.

## Jobs to be done

### Application author exposing an MCP server

> I want to declare tools, resources, prompts, tasks, context, auth, and policy once, then serve them over supported transports without manually managing official-SDK lifecycle or duplicating validation.

### Application author consuming MCP

> I want to connect to a local or remote server, authorize safely when required, use typed capability APIs, handle lifecycle/errors consistently, and avoid writing my own transport and token code.

### Product team protecting compatibility

> I want manifests, diffs, semantic scenarios, auth matrices, and official conformance to run against the same server behavior users exercise, with redacted artifacts I can review in CI.

### Developer diagnosing interoperability

> I want to see discovery, registration, authorization, callback, token, initialization, capabilities, requests, notifications, and tasks as one timeline, then export the failure as a reproducible regression.

### Platform team composing identity

> I want AuthFn or another provider to authenticate subjects and enforce application policy without forcing McpFn to become a second user-management system.

## Product principles

1. **One headless engine, many surfaces.** Client SDK, test runner, CLI, and inspector should share connection, auth, capability, operation, event, and diagnostic contracts.
2. **Official SDK below, application contract above.** McpFn should not fork MCP protocol behavior.
3. **Small happy path, explicit security path.** Routine setup should be concise; tenancy, permissions, confirmation, secret storage, redirect policy, and authorization-server choices must remain visible.
4. **Auth is a lifecycle, not a header.** Discovery, registration, browser handoff, callback, token refresh, revocation, and persistence need first-class state and diagnostics.
5. **Deterministic simulation and live proof are different products.** Provider-shaped fixtures catch regressions; scheduled live smokes catch deployment/provider drift; neither should impersonate the other.
6. **Inspectability is designed into the engine.** A future inspector should not require adding tracing after the fact.
7. **Adapters compose ownership.** AuthFn, DataFn, Super Console, and consumer-specific policy should integrate through narrow contracts.
8. **Compatibility is broader than schemas.** Descriptions, annotations, capabilities, auth behavior, side effects, approvals, and result meaning all affect agents.

## Relationship to AuthFn and shared OAuth packages

### What to learn from AuthFn

AuthFn demonstrates a strong Superfunctions product pattern:

* a side-effect-free declaration object;
* runtime dependencies supplied when creating the server;
* typed client APIs;
* plugin composition;
* generic provider interfaces;
* framework-neutral Web Standard HTTP boundaries;
* clear ownership of sessions, CSRF, hooks, storage, observability, and admin adapters.

McpFn should emulate this developer experience where it improves clarity.

### What can be reused

The shared Superfunctions OAuth packages already provide reusable client-side primitives for provider descriptors, PKCE/state, redirect allowlists, token endpoint transport, refresh/revoke, state stores, encrypted token vaults, route adapters, and deterministic fixtures. These are valuable building blocks for an MCP OAuth client lifecycle.

AuthFn also exposes a generic `AuthProvider<AuthSession>` seam that can authenticate an incoming request and return a trusted subject/session. An McpFn server adapter can map that subject and authorized scopes into MCP request context or official-SDK `AuthInfo`.

### What remains McpFn-specific

MCP authorization adds domain-specific orchestration that generic OAuth packages should not guess:

* handling `WWW-Authenticate` protected-resource challenges;
* fetching RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata;
* selecting and validating authorization-server metadata;
* choosing between pre-registration, DCR, and Client ID Metadata Documents;
* reconciling MCP host callback behavior and native/loopback redirect rules;
* applying resource indicators and MCP scopes;
* connecting or retrying the MCP transport after authorization;
* reporting the precise phase that failed;
* turning a real failure into a reusable MCP regression fixture.

### Role 3 ownership decision and AuthFn boundary

AuthFn's social OAuth plugin is an OAuth client for user sign-in. It is not an OAuth authorization server for arbitrary MCP clients.

{"id":"MCP-2","title":"Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform","description":"## Executive summary

Evolve McpFn from its current server-runtime and test-harness foundation into the batteries-included MCP application SDK and quality platform for Superfunctions. An application should be able to add a production MCP server or client with a small, typed McpFn integration, then use the same McpFn engine for deterministic regression coverage, official conformance, diagnostics, and a future interactive inspector.

This is a product-direction issue, not an OAuth hotfix. It preserves the official MCP SDK as the protocol implementation, composes existing Superfunctions/AuthFn boundaries where they fit, and makes MCP-specific discovery, authorization interoperability, connection lifecycle, testing, and inspection first-class McpFn responsibilities.

**Role 3 ownership decision:** McpFn owns the MCP-specific authorization-server compatibility layer presented by hosted MCP servers: protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, pre-registration/DCR/Client ID Metadata Document normalization, compatible-flow negotiation, redirect validation, PKCE/resource/scope requirements, and MCP-shaped authorization errors. AuthFn or an external authorization system continues to own identities, login, sessions, consent policy, signing keys, token authority, and durable security state.

## Problem or opportunity

The current code establishes a substantial foundation:

* `@mcpfn/core` provides an official-SDK server runtime, registry, tools/resources/prompts/tasks, MCP Apps contracts, canonical manifests, compatibility diffing, request-derived context, and stdio/Streamable HTTP support.
* `@mcpfn/auth` provides RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, bearer verification, audience/resource checks, and scope enforcement.
* `@mcpfn/testing` provides an in-memory test client, manifest assertions, semantic scenarios, auth matrices, a mock OAuth authorization server, a browser PKCE fixture, generic host profiles, and the pinned official conformance runner.
* `@mcpfn/cli` exposes manifest, validate, diff, test, and conformance commands.
* `@mcpfn/datafn` generates deny-by-default DataFn-backed tools.
* LangFn, MemoryFn, ProbeFn, and Super Console demonstrate server-side consumption on `next`; the open `dev` port deliberately excludes several consumer migrations from its release proof.

That foundation does not yet satisfy the intended McpFn product contract:

* there is no production McpFn client SDK; `McpFnTestClient` is in-memory and coupled to `McpFnServer`;
* LangFn therefore carries its own official-SDK client, HTTP/stdio transports, pagination, result normalization, connection lifecycle, and error mapping;
* `@mcpfn/auth` intentionally stops at the resource-server boundary and does not perform protected-resource discovery, authorization-server selection, client registration/metadata negotiation, PKCE, browser handoff, callback validation, token exchange/refresh/revocation, or secure token persistence;
* current OAuth fixtures validate a controlled happy path but do not model enough provider- and host-shaped redirect, discovery, registration, and metadata behavior to catch the recent `redirect_uri is not registered for this client` class of regression early;
* regression commands are primarily McpFn-native/in-memory today, while transport-neutral external-server work is separately tracked by <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>;
* the documentation explicitly places product-level inspector/evaluation UIs outside the current scope;
* Super Console's MCP page inventories administrative tools and clients but is not an interactive MCP protocol inspector.

The opportunity is to make these pieces one coherent platform instead of requiring each consumer to assemble production client behavior, OAuth interoperability, test adapters, diagnostics, and inspection independently.

## Expected outcome

A TypeScript application can:

1. declare and serve a protocol-correct MCP surface with a concise McpFn server SDK;
2. connect to local or remote MCP servers with a production McpFn client SDK;
3. enable MCP-specific OAuth discovery and authorization with safe defaults and explicit policy hooks;
4. compose AuthFn or another identity/authorization system without reimplementing generic user authentication;
5. run the same manifest, semantic, auth, transport, and official-conformance engine in tests and CI;
6. inspect a connection interactively through a future McpFn inspector that consumes the same client/session/diagnostic contracts.

Consumer-owned domain semantics, tenancy, permissions, secrets, and approval policy remain explicit.

## Goals

* Define a stable, minimal client/server developer experience and package model.
* Add a production client runtime for stdio and Streamable HTTP, including capability negotiation, pagination, lifecycle, notifications, client-mediated features, typed result/error handling, cancellation, and reconnect policy.
* Add MCP-specific OAuth client orchestration: protected-resource discovery, authorization-server metadata, supported client registration/metadata modes, PKCE, browser handoff, callback validation, resource indicators, token exchange/refresh/revocation, and pluggable secure persistence.
* Define a provider-neutral server auth seam plus first-class AuthFn/shared-OAuth adapters; keep AuthFn optional.
* Add a hosted-server authorization adapter so applications such as Skillplane delegate MCP-specific client registration, metadata compatibility, redirect matching, and authorization-request validation to McpFn instead of retaining product-local implementations.
* Reuse the official MCP SDK and Superfunctions OAuth/storage primitives instead of creating parallel protocol, state, token, or encryption implementations.
* Generalize the test client into a shared target/session engine usable by in-memory, stdio, remote HTTP, CLI, CI, and the future inspector.
* Add provider- and host-shaped deterministic interoperability profiles that cover redirect URI registration, loopback callbacks, metadata extensions, issuer/resource validation, refresh/revocation, and negative paths.
* Keep official MCP conformance complementary to McpFn contract, semantic, auth, and product smoke coverage.
* Provide redacted, structured diagnostics that identify whether a failure occurred during discovery, registration, authorization, callback, token exchange, MCP initialization, capability negotiation, or a product scenario.
* Establish a phased inspector roadmap built on the shared engine rather than a separate implementation.
* Publish migration paths for current Superfunctions consumers and verify installed-package behavior in release automation.

## Non-goals

* Reimplement JSON-RPC, MCP lifecycle, transports, or the official MCP conformance suite.
* Make AuthFn mandatory or duplicate its user/session/plugin model.
* Treat AuthFn's social-login OAuth client as an MCP authorization server.
* Reimplement generic user identity, login, sessions, consent policy, signing-key management, or durable token authority inside McpFn; these remain AuthFn, application, or external-authorization-system responsibilities.
* Require McpFn to ship a standalone generic authorization server when an adapter over an existing token authority can satisfy the hosted MCP contract.
* Auto-expose an application's domain model, infer permissions, or move tenancy/authorization policy into tool arguments.
* Promise every MCP host or authorization provider behaves identically.
* Treat a green unit, conformance, or mock-browser suite as proof of live deployment interoperability.
* Deliver the full inspector UI in the first implementation phase.
* Migrate Skillplane or other consumers inside this issue; consumer adoption remains separately tracked.

## Acceptance criteria

* A documented package/API decision defines the stable roles of core, server, client, auth, testing, CLI, adapters, and future inspector surfaces.
* A minimal server example and a minimal client example each require only application configuration, domain handlers, and explicit policy hooks—not hand-written MCP lifecycle code.
* The production client connects over stdio and Streamable HTTP and exercises tools, resources, prompts, tasks, notifications, and negotiated client-mediated features through the official SDK.
* The client supports MCP authorization discovery through a pluggable OAuth lifecycle and storage contract, with structured phase-specific errors and redacted diagnostics.
* OAuth regression coverage includes fixed web callbacks, native/loopback callbacks with dynamic ports, exact registered redirect handling, client metadata/DCR variants, PKCE/state replay protection, issuer/resource checks, token endpoint auth-method negotiation, refresh rotation, revocation, denial, expiry, and unsupported-grant classification.
* The recent redirect-registration failure class is reproducible as a deterministic regression that fails when generated authorization requests and registered client metadata diverge.
* A hosted MCP server can delegate all MCP-specific authorization interoperability to McpFn while supplying identity, consent, authorization policy, signing, and storage adapters; consumer code does not parse client metadata, negotiate registration modes, compare redirect URIs, enforce PKCE, or map MCP-specific authorization errors.
* Independently configured Claude-shaped and ChatGPT-shaped end-to-end fixtures complete valid authorization-code + PKCE flows; deliberately incompatible metadata and unregistered callbacks fail with phase-accurate errors.
* The implementation inventories overlapping McpFn, LangFn, shared OAuth, AuthFn, and consumer authorization code; generic PKCE/state/HTTP/storage/redaction primitives are reused, and replaced product-local paths are removed or explicitly deprecated with no parallel production writer.
* McpFn exposes a documented AuthFn integration that maps authenticated subjects/scopes into trusted server context while leaving token issuance/authorization-server policy behind an explicit adapter.
* Generic OAuth state, transport, and encrypted token-storage behavior is reused from the shared Superfunctions packages where compatible; any MCP-specific fork is justified in the architecture document.
* The same target/session engine supports McpFn-native in-memory tests and transport-neutral stdio/HTTP targets without requiring external servers to adopt McpFn server types.
* CLI and programmatic APIs produce bounded, machine-readable, secret-redacted reports with stable exit behavior.
* <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>'s external regression/conformance work plugs into the shared engine and is not duplicated.
* An inspector contract and thin initial shell can discover capabilities, run operations, observe notifications/tasks, visualize auth/discovery phases, and export a reproducible redacted test case using the same client engine.
* Release gates verify package exports, packed-package installation, representative client/server round trips, OAuth browser coverage, manifest/scenario coverage, official conformance, and explicitly named consumer coverage.
* Documentation distinguishes deterministic local proof, official conformance, provider-shaped simulations, controlled live-provider smoke tests, and deployed production proof.

## Dependencies and risks

* Related foundation: <issue id="a44566ef-0f0a-4aa5-b5fa-abe7c38032c3" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-19/mcpfn-init">SFN-19</issue>.
* Related transport-neutral testing work: <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>.
* Skillplane adoption remains in <issue id="aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage">SKI-6</issue>.
* The official MCP SDK and conformance runner evolve; version support and upgrade policy must be explicit.
* Browser and desktop callback environments differ in redirect and loopback behavior.
* DCR, client metadata documents, pre-registration, and enterprise-managed authorization require different policy and security postures.
* Token storage, refresh concurrency, revocation, logging, and exported inspector traces can leak credentials unless redaction and storage boundaries are designed first.
* Current `next` and the open `dev` port do not prove the same consumer coverage; release evidence must name the exact branch/package/consumer scope.
* A convenience API can accidentally obscure tenancy, authorization, confirmation, and destructive-operation controls if those hooks are not explicit.
* Package reshaping before a stable release can create migration cost; compatibility aliases and staged deprecations may be needed.
* Leaving product-local MCP authorization implementations active beside McpFn would create divergent role-3 behavior. Migration gates must verify a single production path and name every retained compatibility shim.

## Open questions

* Should the package model add `@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/server`, or keep server APIs in `@mcpfn/core` with a new client package?
* Which underlying authorization-server and token-authority adapters ship first, given the fixed ownership rule that McpFn owns the MCP compatibility profile while generic identity and token authority remain external?
* Should AuthFn integration live in `@mcpfn/auth`, a dedicated adapter package, or AuthFn itself?
* Which shared OAuth primitives can be reused unchanged for MCP client authorization, and where are MCP-specific discovery/registration semantics required?
* Which runtime targets are required initially: Node only, browser, edge/Workers, desktop/native, or a staged subset?
* Is the future inspector a standalone McpFn app/package, a Super Console module, or both through a shared headless engine?
* Which named host/provider profiles are deterministic fixtures, and which live-provider checks run only on a controlled schedule?
* What compatibility guarantees apply to manifests, diagnostics, scenario files, stored credentials, and inspector exports before 1.0?

* `@mcpfn/core` provides an official-SDK server runtime, registry, tools/resources/prompts/tasks, MCP Apps contracts, canonical manifests, compatibility diffing, request-derived context, and stdio/Streamable HTTP support.
* `@mcpfn/auth` provides RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, bearer verification, audience/resource checks, and scope enforcement.
* `@mcpfn/testing` provides an in-memory test client, manifest assertions, semantic scenarios, auth matrices, a mock OAuth authorization server, a browser PKCE fixture, generic host profiles, and the pinned official conformance runner.
* `@mcpfn/cli` exposes manifest, validate, diff, test, and conformance commands.
* `@mcpfn/datafn` generates deny-by-default DataFn-backed tools.
* LangFn, MemoryFn, ProbeFn, and Super Console demonstrate server-side consumption on `next`; the open `dev` port deliberately excludes several consumer migrations from its release proof.

That foundation does not yet satisfy the intended McpFn product contract:

* there is no production McpFn client SDK; `McpFnTestClient` is in-memory and coupled to `McpFnServer`;
* LangFn therefore carries its own official-SDK client, HTTP/stdio transports, pagination, result normalization, connection lifecycle, and error mapping;
* `@mcpfn/auth` intentionally stops at the resource-server boundary and does not perform protected-resource discovery, authorization-server selection, client registration/metadata negotiation, PKCE, browser handoff, callback validation, token exchange/refresh/revocation, or secure token persistence;
* current OAuth fixtures validate a controlled happy path but do not model enough provider- and host-shaped redirect, discovery, registration, and metadata behavior to catch the recent `redirect_uri is not registered for this client` class of regression early;
* regression commands are primarily McpFn-native/in-memory today, while transport-neutral external-server work is separately tracked by <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>;
* the documentation explicitly places product-level inspector/evaluation UIs outside the current scope;
* Super Console's MCP page inventories administrative tools and clients but is not an interactive MCP protocol inspector.

The opportunity is to make these pieces one coherent platform instead of requiring each consumer to assemble production client behavior, OAuth interoperability, test adapters, diagnostics, and inspection independently.

## Expected outcome

A TypeScript application can:

1. declare and serve a protocol-correct MCP surface with a concise McpFn server SDK;
2. connect to local or remote MCP servers with a production McpFn client SDK;
3. enable MCP-specific OAuth discovery and authorization with safe defaults and explicit policy hooks;
4. compose AuthFn or another identity/authorization system without reimplementing generic user authentication;
5. run the same manifest, semantic, auth, transport, and official-conformance engine in tests and CI;
6. inspect a connection interactively through a future McpFn inspector that consumes the same client/session/diagnostic contracts.

Consumer-owned domain semantics, tenancy, permissions, secrets, and approval policy remain explicit.

## Goals

* Define a stable, minimal client/server developer experience and package model.
* Add a production client runtime for stdio and Streamable HTTP, including capability negotiation, pagination, lifecycle, notifications, client-mediated features, typed result/error handling, cancellation, and reconnect policy.
* Add MCP-specific OAuth client orchestration: protected-resource discovery, authorization-server metadata, supported client registration/metadata modes, PKCE, browser handoff, callback validation, resource indicators, token exchange/refresh/revocation, and pluggable secure persistence.
* Define a provider-neutral server auth seam plus first-class AuthFn/shared-OAuth adapters; keep AuthFn optional.
* Add a hosted-server authorization adapter so applications such as Skillplane delegate MCP-specific client registration, metadata compatibility, redirect matching, and authorization-request validation to McpFn instead of retaining product-local implementations.
* Reuse the official MCP SDK and Superfunctions OAuth/storage primitives instead of creating parallel protocol, state, token, or encryption implementations.
* Generalize the test client into a shared target/session engine usable by in-memory, stdio, remote HTTP, CLI, CI, and the future inspector.
* Add provider- and host-shaped deterministic interoperability profiles that cover redirect URI registration, loopback callbacks, metadata extensions, issuer/resource validation, refresh/revocation, and negative paths.
* Keep official MCP conformance complementary to McpFn contract, semantic, auth, and product smoke coverage.
* Provide redacted, structured diagnostics that identify whether a failure occurred during discovery, registration, authorization, callback, token exchange, MCP initialization, capability negotiation, or a product scenario.
* Establish a phased inspector roadmap built on the shared engine rather than a separate implementation.
* Publish migration paths for current Superfunctions consumers and verify installed-package behavior in release automation.

## Non-goals

* Reimplement JSON-RPC, MCP lifecycle, transports, or the official MCP conformance suite.
* Make AuthFn mandatory or duplicate its user/session/plugin model.
* Treat AuthFn's social-login OAuth client as an MCP authorization server.
* Reimplement generic user identity, login, sessions, consent policy, signing-key management, or durable token authority inside McpFn; these remain AuthFn, application, or external-authorization-system responsibilities.
* Require McpFn to ship a standalone generic authorization server when an adapter over an existing token authority can satisfy the hosted MCP contract.
* Auto-expose an application's domain model, infer permissions, or move tenancy/authorization policy into tool arguments.
* Promise every MCP host or authorization provider behaves identically.
* Treat a green unit, conformance, or mock-browser suite as proof of live deployment interoperability.
* Deliver the full inspector UI in the first implementation phase.
* Migrate Skillplane or other consumers inside this issue; consumer adoption remains separately tracked.

## Acceptance criteria

* A documented package/API decision defines the stable roles of core, server, client, a

* A minimal server example and a minimal client example each require only application configuration, domain handlers, and explicit policy hooks—not hand-written MCP lifecycle code.
* The production client connects over stdio and Streamable HTTP and exercises tools, resources, prompts, tasks, notifications, and negotiated client-mediated features through the official SDK.
* The client supports MCP authorization discovery through a pluggable OAuth lifecycle and storage contract, with structured phase-specific errors and redacted diagnostics.
* OAuth regression coverage includes fixed web callbacks, native/loopback callbacks with dynamic ports, exact registered redirect handling, client metadata/DCR variants, PKCE/state replay protection, issuer/resource checks, token endpoint auth-method negotiation, refresh rotation, revocation, denial, expiry, and unsupported-grant classification.
* The recent redirect-registration failure class is reproducible as a deterministic regression that fails when generated authorization requests and registered client metadata diverge.
* A hosted MCP server can delegate all MCP-specific authorization interoperability to McpFn while supplying identity, consent, authorization policy, signing, and storage adapters; consumer code does not parse client metadata, negotiate registration modes, compare redirect URIs, enforce PKCE, or map MCP-specific authorization errors.
* Independently configured Claude-shaped and ChatGPT-shaped end-to-end fixtures complete valid authorization-code + PKCE flows; deliberately incompatible metadata and unregistered callbacks fail with phase-accurate errors.
* The implementation inventories overlapping McpFn, LangFn, shared OAuth, AuthFn, and consumer authorization code; generic PKCE/state/HTTP/storage/redaction primitives are reused, and replaced product-local paths are removed or explicitly deprecated with no parallel production writer.
* McpFn exposes a documented AuthFn integration that maps authenticated subjects/scopes into trusted server context while leaving token issuance/authorization-server policy behind an explicit adapter.
* Generic OAuth state, transport, and encrypted token-storage behavior is reused from the shared Superfunctions packages where compatible; any MCP-specific fork is justified in the architecture document.
* The same target/session engine supports McpFn-native in-memory tests and transport-neutral stdio/HTTP targets without requiring external servers to adopt McpFn server types.
* CLI and programmatic APIs produce bounded, machine-readable, secret-redacted reports with stable exit behavior.
* <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>'s external regression/conformance work plugs into the shared engine and is not duplicated.
* An inspector contract and thin initial shell can discover capabilities, run operations, observe notifications/tasks, visualize auth/discovery phases, and export a reproducible redacted test case using the same client engine.
* Release gates verify package exports, packed-package installation, representative client/server round trips, OAuth browser coverage, manifest/scenario coverage, official conformance, and explicitly named consumer coverage.
* Documentation distinguishes deterministic local proof, official conformance, provider-shaped simulations, controlled live-provider smoke tests, and deployed production proof.

## Dependencies and risks

* Related foundation: <issue id="a44566ef-0f0a-4aa5-b5fa-abe7c38032c3" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-19/mcpfn-init">SFN-19</issue>.
* Related transport-neutral testing work: <issue id="6283bb40-0de7-4875-a6f1-31a5016044c8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-1/enable-transport-neutral-mcpfn-regression-and-conformance-testing">MCP-1</issue>.
* Skillplane adoption remains in <issue id="aaf7021f-756f-4919-ad1c-830c2fa250f8" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage">SKI-6</issue>.
* The official MCP SDK and conformance runner evolve; version support and upgrade policy must be explicit.
* Browser and desktop callback environments differ in redirect and loopback behavior.
* DCR, client metadata documents, pre-registration, and enterprise-managed authorization require different policy and security postures.
* Token storage, refresh concurrency, revocation, logging, and exported inspector traces can leak credentials unless redaction and storage boundaries are designed first.
* Current `next` and the open `dev` port do not prove the same consumer coverage; release evidence must name the exact branch/package/consumer scope.
* A convenience API can accidentally obscure tenancy, authorization, confirmation, and destructive-operation controls if those hooks are not explicit.
* Package reshaping before a stable release can create migration cost; compatibility aliases and staged deprecations may be needed.
* Leaving product-local MCP authorization implementations active beside McpFn would create divergent role-3 behavior. Migration gates must verify a single production path and name every retained compatibility shim.

## Open questions

* Should the package model add `@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/server`, or keep server APIs in `@mcpfn/core` with a new client package?
* Which underlying authorization-server and token-authority adapters ship first, given the fixed ownership rule that McpFn owns the MCP compatibility profile while generic identity and token authority remain external?
* Should AuthFn integration live in `@mcpfn/auth`, a dedicated adapter package, or AuthFn itself?
* Which shared OAuth primitives can be reused unchanged for MCP client authorization, and where are MCP-specific discovery/registration semantics required?
* Which runtime targets are required initially: Node only, browser, edge/Workers, desktop/native, or a staged subset?
* Is the future inspector a standalone McpFn app/package, a Super Console module, or both through a shared headless engine?
* Which named host/provider profiles are deterministic fixtures, and which live-provider checks run only on a controlled schedule?
* What compatibility guarantees apply to manifests, diagnostics, scenario files, stored credentials, and inspector exports before 1.0?

1	# McpFn
     2	
     3	McpFn is the Superfunctions layer for building and keeping Model Context Protocol servers regression-free. It uses the official MCP SDK for protocol and transport behavior, then adds validated tools, resources, prompts, task execution, client-mediated features, OAuth resource-server security, MCP Apps contracts, deterministic manifests, compatibility diffs, semantic scenarios, and a safe DataFn adapter.
     4	
     5	## Packages
     6	
     7	| Package | Purpose |
     8	| --- | --- |
     9	| `@mcpfn/core` | Official-SDK runtime, tools/resources/prompts/tasks, client-mediated features, MCP Apps contracts, manifests, and compatibility diffing |
    10	| `@mcpfn/client` | Production stdio/Streamable HTTP targets, lifecycle-safe sessions, complete inventories, tasks, OAuth callback completion, and redacted phase diagnostics |
    11	| `@mcpfn/auth` | OAuth client persistence and callback policy, discovery diagnostics, hosted authorization compatibility, RFC 9728 resource protection, and generic auth-provider composition |
    12	| `@mcpfn/testing` | The production client exposed as a fixture, auth regression matrices, named host-shaped OAuth fixtures, local/external target suites, scenarios, Playwright, and conformance orchestration |
    13	| `@mcpfn/inspector` | Headless inventory, capability execution, redacted timelines, and sanitized scenario export over the production client |
    14	| `@mcpfn/datafn` | Deny-by-default generation of bounded MCP tools from a DataFn server executor |
    15	| `@mcpfn/cli` | Contract, local/remote target testing, inspection, authorization discovery diagnostics, and official conformance commands with stable CI exit codes |
    16	
    17	All client-side surfaces share `@mcpfn/client`; tests, the inspector, and CLI do
    18	not carry private transport or protocol implementations. McpFn's inspector is
    19	headless so product UIs can compose it without becoming runtime dependencies.
    20	
    21	## Quick start
    22	
    23	```ts
    24	import {
    25	  McpFnRegistry,
    26	  createMcpFnServer,
    27	  structuredResult,
    28	} from "@mcpfn/core";
    29	
    30	// Replace this example with your application's published-skill lookup.
    31	const resolvePublishedSkill = async (slug: string) => ({ slug });
    32	
    33	const registry = new McpFnRegistry().register({
    34	  name: "skill_get",
    35	  description: "Resolve one published skill by slug.",
    36	  inputSchema: {
    37	    type: "object",
    38	    properties: { slug: { type: "string", minLength: 1 } },
    39	    required: ["slug"],
    40	    additionalProperties: false,
    41	  },
    42	  outputSchema: {
    43	    type: "object",
    44	    properties: { skill: { type: "object" } },
    45	    required: ["skill"],
    46	    additionalProperties: false,
    47	  },
    48	  annotations: {
    49	    readOnlyHint: true,
    50	    destructiveHint: false,
    51	    idempotentHint: true,
    52	    openWorldHint: false,
    53	  },
    54	  handler: async ({ slug }) =>
    55	    structuredResult({ skill: await resolvePublishedSkill(String(slug)) }),
    56	});
    57	
    58	const server = createMcpFnServer({
    59	  info: { name: "skillplane", version: "1.0.0" },
    60	  registry,
    61	  transports: ["stdio", "streamable-http"],
    62	});
    63	
    64	await server.serveStdio();
    65	```
    66	
    67	The handler receives only schema-valid arguments. If an output schema is declared, McpFn also validates `structuredContent` before returning it. Domain errors with a string `code` retain that code in the MCP error result.
    68	
    69	## Regression workflow
    70	
    71	Commit a manifest baseline and semantic scenarios with the MCP server:
    72	
    73	```sh
    74	mcpfn manifest ./src/mcp/server.ts --output ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    75	mcpfn validate ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    76	mcpfn diff ./mcpfn.manifest.json ./candidate.manifest.json --fail-on-behavioral
    77	mcpfn test ./src/mcp/server.ts ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts --output ./mcpfn-report.json
    78	mcpfn test-target https://api.example.com/mcp ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts
    79	mcpfn inspect https://api.example.com/mcp --output ./mcpfn-inspection.json
    80	mcpfn auth-diagnose https://api.example.com/mcp
    81	mcpfn conformance http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --suite active
    82	```
    83	
    84	The manifest catches tool, resource, template, prompt, task, extension, client-requirement, protocol-version, and transport changes. Scenarios catch business behavior. Host profiles expose feature mismatches. The official conformance runner catches wire-protocol behavior. None of those layers substitutes for the others.
    85	
    86	The conformance subcommand pins the reviewed official runner version and requires Node.js 22 or newer. Other McpFn commands support Node.js 18.18 or newer.
    87	
    88	Run `npm run gate:mcpfn-release` from this repository for the complete package, example, migration, and packability gate.
    89	
    90	The examples include a declaration-backed calculator server, stdio entrypoint,
    91	Streamable HTTP entrypoint, production client, semantic scenarios, and committed
    92	manifest under `mcpfn/examples`.
    93	
    94	## Authorization and MCP Apps
    95	
    96	Wrap `server.createWebStandardHandler()` with
    97	`createOAuthResourceServerHandler()` from `@mcpfn/auth`. For clients, use
    98	`McpFnOAuthClientProvider`; it delegates discovery, DCR, PKCE, token exchange,
    99	and refresh mechanics to the official SDK, correlates callback state, validates
   100	redirects before browser launch, defaults to memory-only credentials, and
   101	supports encrypted application-provided persistence. Hosted applications can
   102	compose their existing login, consent, signing, and token authority through
   103	`createMcpAuthorizationCompatibilityHandler()` instead of creating a second
   104	identity system. Existing `@superfunctions/oauth-*` packages continue to own
   105	outbound provider connections.
   106	
   107	Use `@mcpfn/testing/auth` to run the common missing, invalid, valid, insufficient-scope, expired, wrong-resource, and revoked credential matrix. Use `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` for a real authorization-code + PKCE browser flow, refresh rotation, revocation, callback capture, and extensible Client ID Metadata fixtures. An application such as Skillplane supplies only its API-key/token lifecycle adapter, authorization endpoint, login setup, and product-specific access assertions.
   108	
   109	Use `createMcpAppResource()` and `mcpAppToolMetadata()` for `ui://` HTML resources. McpFn validates the MCP App MIME type, CSP metadata, visibility, and tool-to-resource links. It does not implement a browser iframe host.
   110	
   111	## DataFn boundary
   112	
   113	`@mcpfn/datafn` is useful when a domain operation really is a bounded projection of DataFn query/mutation semantics. A resource must be explicitly named, returned fields are fixed, filter/sort fields are allowlisted, and writes require explicit fields plus a caller-supplied `mutationId`. Authentication, namespace, actor, and `clientId` values come from trusted server context.
   114	
   115	Do not auto-publish an entire DataFn schema. Skillplane-style operations such as version resolution, access grants, audit workflows, or asset delivery should remain explicit domain tools even if they call DataFn internally.
   116	
   117	## Documentation
   118	
   119	- [Architecture](./ARCHITECTURE.md)
   120	- [Adoption inventory](./ADOPTION.md)
   121	- [Testing and CI](./TESTING.md)
   122	- [Migration guide](./MIGRATION.md)
   123	- [Core API](./core/README.md)
   124	- [OAuth resource server](./auth/README.md)
   125	- [DataFn adapter](./datafn/README.md)

     1	# Testing and CI
     2	
     3	A regression-free MCP project needs five independent layers.
     4	
     5	| Layer | What it catches | McpFn surface |
     6	| --- | --- | --- |
     7	| Unit/domain | Handler logic, authorization, persistence, policy | Existing package tests |
     8	| Contract | Tools, resources, prompts, tasks, extensions, host requirements | Hashed manifest plus `mcpfn diff` |
     9	| Semantic protocol | Real client/server calls and stable business envelopes | `@mcpfn/testing` scenarios |
    10	| Authentication | API keys, OAuth challenges, scopes, audience, expiry, revocation, PKCE, refresh, and client metadata | `@mcpfn/testing/auth` and `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` |
    11	| Protocol conformance | Initialization, JSON-RPC, transport, and MCP specification behavior | Official `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance` via `mcpfn conformance` |
    12	
    13	## Contract baseline
    14	
    15	Generate a candidate manifest from a module whose default export is a `McpFnServer`, an async factory returning one, a `McpFnRegistry`, or an existing manifest:
    16	
    17	```sh

    41	  },
    42	  outputSchema: {

    44	    properties: { skill: { type: "object" } },
    45	    required: ["skill"],
    46	    additionalProperties: false,

    66	
    67	The handler receives only schema-valid arguments. If an output schema is declared, McpFn also validates `structuredContent` before returning it. Domain errors with a string `code` retain that code in the MCP error result.
    68	
    69	## Regression workflow
    70	
    71	Commit a manifest baseline and semantic scenarios with the MCP server:
    72	
    73	```sh
    74	mcpfn manifest ./src/mcp/server.ts --output ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    75	mcpfn validate ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    76	mcpfn diff ./mcpfn.manifest.json ./candidate.manifest.json --fail-on-behavioral
    77	mcpfn test ./src/mcp/server.ts ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts --output ./mcpfn-report.json
    78	mcpfn test-target https://api.example.com/mcp ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts
    79	mcpfn inspect https://api.example.com/mcp --output ./mcpfn-inspection.json
    80	mcpfn auth-diagnose https://api.example.com/mcp
    81	mcpfn conformance http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --suite active
    82	```
    83	
    84	The manifest catches tool, resource, template, prompt, task, extension, client-requirement, protocol-version, and transport changes. Scenarios catch business behavior. Host profiles expose feature mismatches. The official conformance runner catches wire-protocol behavior. None of those layers substitutes for the others.
    85	
    86	The conformance subcommand pins the reviewed official runner version and requires Node.js 22 or newer. Other McpFn commands support Node.js 18.18 or newer.
    87	
    88	Run `npm run gate:mcpfn-release` from this repository for the complete package, example, migration, and packability gate.
    89	
    90	The examples include a declaration-backed calculator server, stdio entrypoint,
    91	Streamable HTTP entrypoint, production client, semantic scenarios, and committed
    92	manifest under `mcpfn/examples`.
    93	
    94	## Authorization and MCP Apps
    95	
    96	Wrap `server.createWebStandardHandler()` with
    97	`createOAuthResourceServerHandler()` from `@mcpfn/auth`. For clients, use
    98	`McpFnOAuthClientProvider`; it delegates discovery, DCR, PKCE, token exchange,
    99	and refresh mechanics to the official SDK, correlates callback state, validates
   100	redirects before browser launch, defaults to memory-only credentials, and
   101	supports encrypted application-provided persistence. Hosted applications can
   102	compose their existing login, consent, signing, and token authority through
   103	`createMcpAuthorizationCompatibilityHandler()` instead of creating a second
   104	identity system. Existing `@superfunctions/oauth-*` packages continue to own
   105	outbound provider connections.
   106	
   107	Use `@mcpfn/testing/auth` to run the common missing, invalid, valid, insufficient-scope, expired, wrong-resource, and revoked credential matrix. Use `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` for a real authorization-code + PKCE browser flow, refresh rotation, revocation, callback capture, and extensible Client ID Metadata fixtures. An application such as Skillplane supplies only its API-key/token lifecycle adapter, authorization endpoint, login setup, and product-specific access assertions.
   108	
   109	Use `createMcpAppResource()` and `mcpAppToolMetadata()` for `ui://` HTML resources. McpFn validates the MCP App MIME type, CSP metadata, visibility, and tool-to-resource links. It does not implement a browser iframe host.
   110	
   111	## DataFn boundary
   112	
   113	`@mcpfn/datafn` is useful when a domain operation really is a bounded projection of DataFn query/mutation semantics. A resource must be explicitly named, returned fields are fixed, filter/sort fields are allowlisted, and writes require explicit fields plus a caller-supplied `mutationId`. Authentication, namespace, actor, and `clientId` values come from trusted server context.
   114	
   115	Do not auto-publish an entire DataFn schema. Skillplane-style operations such as version resolution, access grants, audit workflows, or asset delivery should remain explicit domain tools even if they call DataFn internally.
   116

   122	- [Migration guide](./MIGRATION.md)

     1	# Testing and CI
     2	
     3	A regression-free MCP project needs five independent layers.
     4	
     5	| Layer | What it catches | McpFn surface |
     6	| --- | --- | --- |
     7	| Unit/domain | Handler logic, authorization, persistence, policy | Existing package tests |
     8	| Contract | Tools, resources, prompts, tasks, extensions, host requirements | Hashed manifest plus `mcpfn diff` |
     9	| Semantic protocol | Real client/server calls and stable business envelopes | `@mcpfn/testing` scenarios |
    10	| Authentication | API keys, OAuth challenges, scopes, audience, expiry, revocation, PKCE, refresh, and client metadata | `@mcpfn/testing/auth` and `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` |
    11	| Protocol conformance | Initialization, JSON-RPC, transport, and MCP specification behavior | Official `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance` via `mcpfn conformance` |
    12	
    13	## Contract baseline
    14	
    15	Generate a candidate manifest from a module whose default export is a `McpFnServer`, an async factory returning one, a `McpFnRegistry`, or an existing manifest:
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	mcpfn manifest ./mcp-server.ts --output ./candidate.manifest.json
    19	mcpfn diff ./mcpfn.manifest.json ./candidate.manifest.json --fail-on-behavioral
    20	```
    21	
    22	For a registry export, pass both `--name` and `--version`. Exit code `1` means the diff found a breaking change, or a behavioral change when requested. Exit code `2` means the source or command was invalid.
    23	
    24	Review additive changes before replacing the committed baseline. A compatible diff means old inputs remain structurally accepted; it does not prove the new tool is authorized or semantically correct.
    25	
    26	## Semantic scenarios
    27	
    28	```ts
    29	import type { McpFnScenario } from "@mcpfn/testing";
    30	
    31	export default [
    32	  {
    33	    name: "resolves the published version",
    34	    tool: "skill_get",
    35	    arguments: { slug: "work-linear-issue" },
    36	    expect: {
    37	      isError: false,
    38	      structuredContent: {
    39	        skill: { slug: "work-linear-issue", version: 3 },
    40	      },
    41	      structuredTextParity: true,
    42	    },
    43	  },
    44	] satisfies McpFnScenario[];
    45	```
    46	
    47	`mcpfn test` connects the production McpFn client and server with the official
    48	in-memory transport. `mcpfn test-target` runs the same scenarios against stdio
    49	or Streamable HTTP. Both check or exercise the real capability boundary.
    50	`McpFnTestClient` also exposes resources, prompts, completions, subscriptions,
    51	and experimental task APIs; its `configure` hook installs client-side roots,
    52	sampling, elicitation, and notification handlers before initialization.
    53	
    54	`structuredTextParity` is appropriate only when the text block is JSON representing the same object as `structuredContent`. Human-readable text such as MemoryFn's search summary should be asserted separately.
    55	
    56	For tools with a declared success `outputSchema`, assert error codes by parsing the JSON text block: McpFn intentionally omits structured error content so it cannot be rejected against the success schema.
    57	
    58	## Authentication
    59	
    60	`assertAuthRegressionSuite()` runs the transport-level API-key or OAuth matrix against a caller-provided protected operation. The thin provider adapter maps credential issuance and revocation to the application's existing test support. OAuth runs can enable scope, expiry, resource binding, and revocation capabilities; resource-binding coverage rejects both missing and incorrect resource indicators, and every rejected OAuth request is checked for a protected-resource `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.
    61	
    62	The `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` subpath exports a Playwright `test` extended with `mcpfnOAuth`. Its local server supports authorization-code + PKCE, consent approval and denial, callback capture, one-time codes, refresh rotation, revocation, discovery, client metadata variants, and access-token verification. The extension-grant variants verify that an authorization server accepts a compatible authorization-code client even when its metadata advertises additional JWT-bearer, device-code, or custom grants. Actual unsupported token requests must still return `unsupported_grant_type`.
    63	
    64	Keep application-specific UI selectors, real-provider secrets, workspace authorization, and least-privilege assertions in the application repository. McpFn owns the reusable protocol and credential-lifecycle mechanics.
    65	
    66	## Official conformance
    67	
    68	Start a real Streamable HTTP endpoint, then run:
    69	
    70	```sh
    71	mcpfn conformance http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --suite active
    72	```
    73	
    74	McpFn delegates to the pinned official conformance npm package and returns its exit code. The current pinned runner requires Node.js 22 or newer. Use an expected-failures file only for reviewed, time-bounded exceptions; do not turn new failures into a silent baseline update.
    75	
    76	## Superfunctions release gate
    77	
    78	```sh
    79	npm run gate:mcpfn-release
    80	```
    81	
    82	The gate typechecks, tests, and builds all seven McpFn packages; runs real stdio
    83	and Streamable HTTP round trips, OAuth boundary tests, a real Chromium PKCE
    84	flow, and the official active conformance suite; runs the complete DataFn
    85	server suite; exercises the real CLI; checks package contents; and installs
    86	packed artifacts into a temporary external consumer for ESM and CommonJS
    87	imports. LangFn, MemoryFn, and ProbeFn are not covered by this release gate.
    88	
    89	CI routes a change set made entirely of the McpFn runtime, its DataFn adapter, README, and release metadata through this dedicated Node.js 22 gate. Root package manifests, lockfiles, CI workflows, and the CI planner always run the repository's generic JavaScript job as well as the McpFn gate. This conservative boundary prevents unrelated global changes from gaining coverage merely by being included with McpFn work.
    90	
    91	When publishing manually, release the required `@superfunctions/oauth-*`
    92	versions, then `@mcpfn/core`, `@mcpfn/client`, and `@mcpfn/auth`, followed by
    93	`@mcpfn/testing`, `@mcpfn/inspector`, `@mcpfn/datafn`, and `@mcpfn/cli`. The
    94	repository's package release workflow publishes one selected package at a time;
    95	it does not infer dependency order.
     1	# `@mcpfn/auth`
     2	
     3	OAuth integration for MCP clients, resource servers, and hosted authorization
     4	systems. Protocol mechanics remain in the official MCP SDK.
     5	
     6	```ts
     7	import { createOAuthResourceServerHandler } from "@mcpfn/auth";
     8	
     9	const mcp = await server.createWebStandardHandler({ enableJsonResponse: true });
    10	const fetch = createOAuthResourceServerHandler(mcp, {
    11	  resource: "https://api.example.com/mcp",
    12	  authorizationServers: ["https://login.example.com"],
    13	  scopesSupported: ["mcp:read"],
    14	  requiredScopes: ["mcp:read"],
    15	  verifier,
    16	});
    17	```
    18	
    19	Enterprise-managed authorization helpers advertise the stable ID-JAG grant profile in authorization-server metadata and build the request metadata used by supporting clients.
    20	
    21	## Client provider
    22	
    23	`createMcpFnOAuthClientProvider()` implements the official
    24	`OAuthClientProvider`. It validates the requested redirect against registered
    25	metadata before opening a browser, correlates callback state, stores PKCE and
    26	tokens in memory unless an encrypted store is supplied, classifies token
    27	exchange/refresh/revocation diagnostics, and redacts credentials.
    28	
    29	```ts
    30	const provider = createMcpFnOAuthClientProvider({
    31	  redirectUrl: "http://127.0.0.1/callback",
    32	  clientMetadata: {
    33	    redirect_uris: ["http://127.0.0.1/callback"],
    34	    response_types: ["code"],
    35	    grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
    36	  },
    37	  openAuthorization: (url) => browser.open(url),
    38	});
    39	```
    40	
    41	Pass it to `streamableHttpTarget`. Complete interactive authorization with
    42	`client.completeAuthorization({ code, state })`; a missing or mismatched state
    43	fails before token exchange. Dynamic loopback ports are accepted only when the
    44	registered URI omits the port. Other redirect URIs require exact equality.
    45	
    46	## Hosted compatibility
    47	
    48	`createMcpAuthorizationCompatibilityHandler()` publishes authorization-server
    49	metadata and composes DCR, pre-registration, Client ID Metadata Documents,
    50	authorization-code + PKCE request validation, token, and revocation endpoints.
    51	The host application's callbacks remain authoritative for login, consent,
    52	durable clients, code issuance, signing, refresh rotation, and revocation.
    53	External Client ID Metadata Documents require an explicit URL allow-policy.
    54	
    55	`createMcpFnAuthProviderAdapter()` maps a generic `@superfunctions/auth`
    56	session into official MCP `authInfo`, keeping identity, tenant, scopes, and
    57	resources out of model-controlled tool arguments. `auth-diagnose` and
    58	`diagnoseMcpAuthorization()` perform read-only discovery without browser or
    59	credential actions.
