     1	# McpFn
     2	
     3	McpFn is the Superfunctions layer for building and keeping Model Context Protocol servers regression-free. It uses the official MCP SDK for protocol and transport behavior, then adds validated tools, resources, prompts, task execution, client-mediated features, OAuth resource-server security, MCP Apps contracts, deterministic manifests, compatibility diffs, semantic scenarios, and a safe DataFn adapter.
     4	
     5	## Packages
     6	
     7	| Package | Purpose |
     8	| --- | --- |
     9	| `@mcpfn/core` | Official-SDK runtime, tools/resources/prompts/tasks, client-mediated features, MCP Apps contracts, manifests, and compatibility diffing |
    10	| `@mcpfn/client` | Production stdio/Streamable HTTP targets, lifecycle-safe sessions, complete inventories, tasks, OAuth callback completion, and redacted phase diagnostics |
    11	| `@mcpfn/auth` | OAuth client persistence and callback policy, discovery diagnostics, hosted authorization compatibility, RFC 9728 resource protection, and generic auth-provider composition |
    12	| `@mcpfn/testing` | The production client exposed as a fixture, auth regression matrices, named host-shaped OAuth fixtures, local/external target suites, scenarios, Playwright, and conformance orchestration |
    13	| `@mcpfn/inspector` | Headless inventory, capability execution, redacted timelines, and sanitized scenario export over the production client |
    14	| `@mcpfn/datafn` | Deny-by-default generation of bounded MCP tools from a DataFn server executor |
    15	| `@mcpfn/cli` | Contract, local/remote target testing, inspection, authorization discovery diagnostics, and official conformance commands with stable CI exit codes |
    16	
    17	All client-side surfaces share `@mcpfn/client`; tests, the inspector, and CLI do
    18	not carry private transport or protocol implementations. McpFn's inspector is
    19	headless so product UIs can compose it without becoming runtime dependencies.
    20	
    21	## Quick start
    22	
    23	```ts
    24	import {
    25	  McpFnRegistry,
    26	  createMcpFnServer,
    27	  structuredResult,
    28	} from "@mcpfn/core";
    29	
    30	// Replace this example with your application's published-skill lookup.
    31	const resolvePublishedSkill = async (slug: string) => ({ slug });
    32	
    33	const registry = new McpFnRegistry().register({
    34	  name: "skill_get",
    35	  description: "Resolve one published skill by slug.",
    36	  inputSchema: {
    37	    type: "object",
    38	    properties: { slug: { type: "string", minLength: 1 } },
    39	    required: ["slug"],
    40	    additionalProperties: false,
    41	  },
    42	  outputSchema: {
    43	    type: "object",
    44	    properties: { skill: { type: "object" } },
    45	    required: ["skill"],
    46	    additionalProperties: false,
    47	  },
    48	  annotations: {
    49	    readOnlyHint: true,
    50	    destructiveHint: false,
    51	    idempotentHint: true,
    52	    openWorldHint: false,
    53	  },
    54	  handler: async ({ slug }) =>
    55	    structuredResult({ skill: await resolvePublishedSkill(String(slug)) }),
    56	});
    57	
    58	const server = createMcpFnServer({
    59	  info: { name: "skillplane", version: "1.0.0" },
    60	  registry,
    61	  transports: ["stdio", "streamable-http"],
    62	});
    63	
    64	await server.serveStdio();
    65	```
    66	
    67	The handler receives only schema-valid arguments. If an output schema is declared, McpFn also validates `structuredContent` before returning it. Domain errors with a string `code` retain that code in the MCP error result.
    68	
    69	## Regression workflow
    70	
    71	Commit a manifest baseline and semantic scenarios with the MCP server:
    72	
    73	```sh
    74	mcpfn manifest ./src/mcp/server.ts --output ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    75	mcpfn validate ./mcpfn.manifest.json
    76	mcpfn diff ./mcpfn.manifest.json ./candidate.manifest.json --fail-on-behavioral
    77	mcpfn test ./src/mcp/server.ts ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts --output ./mcpfn-report.json
    78	mcpfn test-target https://api.example.com/mcp ./tests/mcp.scenarios.ts
    79	mcpfn inspect https://api.example.com/mcp --output ./mcpfn-inspection.json
    80	mcpfn auth-diagnose https://api.example.com/mcp
    81	mcpfn conformance http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --suite active
    82	```
    83	
    84	The manifest catches tool, resource, template, prompt, task, extension, client-requirement, protocol-version, and transport changes. Scenarios catch business behavior. Host profiles expose feature mismatches. The official conformance runner catches wire-protocol behavior. None of those layers substitutes for the others.
    85	
    86	The conformance subcommand pins the reviewed official runner version and requires Node.js 22 or newer. Other McpFn commands support Node.js 18.18 or newer.
    87	
    88	Run `npm run gate:mcpfn-release` from this repository for the complete package, example, migration, and packability gate.
    89	
    90	The examples include a declaration-backed calculator server, stdio entrypoint,
    91	Streamable HTTP entrypoint, production client, semantic scenarios, and committed
    92	manifest under `mcpfn/examples`.
    93	
    94	## Authorization and MCP Apps
    95	
    96	Wrap `server.createWebStandardHandler()` with
    97	`createOAuthResourceServerHandler()` from `@mcpfn/auth`. For clients, use
    98	`McpFnOAuthClientProvider`; it delegates discovery, DCR, PKCE, token exchange,
    99	and refresh mechanics to the official SDK, correlates callback state, validates
   100	redirects before browser launch, defaults to memory-only credentials, and
   101	supports encrypted application-provided persistence. Hosted applications can
   102	compose their existing login, consent, signing, and token authority through
   103	`createMcpAuthorizationCompatibilityHandler()` instead of creating a second
   104	identity system. Existing `@superfunctions/oauth-*` packages continue to own
   105	outbound provider connections.
   106	
   107	Use `@mcpfn/testing/auth` to run the common missing, invalid, valid, insufficient-scope, expired, wrong-resource, and revoked credential matrix. Use `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` for a real authorization-code + PKCE browser flow, refresh rotation, revocation, callback capture, and extensible Client ID Metadata fixtures. An application such as Skillplane supplies only its API-key/token lifecycle adapter, authorization endpoint, login setup, and product-specific access assertions.
   108	
   109	Use `createMcpAppResource()` and `mcpAppToolMetadata()` for `ui://` HTML resources. McpFn validates the MCP App MIME type, CSP metadata, visibility, and tool-to-resource links. It does not implement a browser iframe host.
   110	
   111	## DataFn boundary
   112	
   113	`@mcpfn/datafn` is useful when a domain operation really is a bounded projection of DataFn query/mutation semantics. A resource must be explicitly named, returned fields are fixed, filter/sort fields are allowlisted, and writes require explicit fields plus a caller-supplied `mutationId`. Authentication, namespace, actor, and `clientId` values come from trusted server context.
   114	
   115	Do not auto-publish an entire DataFn schema. Skillplane-style operations such as version resolution, access grants, audit workflows, or asset delivery should remain explicit domain tools even if they call DataFn internally.

1	# McpFn architecture
     2	
     3	McpFn separates protocol correctness from product correctness and gives every
     4	client-side tool one session engine.
     5	
     6	```text
     7	MCP client
     8	   |
     9	official MCP SDK transports and protocol lifecycle
    10	   |
    11	OAuth resource-server wrapper -> validated authInfo
    12	   |
    13	McpFnServer -> trusted request context and client-mediated requests
    14	   |
    15	McpFnRegistry -> tools/resources/prompts/tasks -> domain handlers
    16	   |                                      |
    17	explicit domain tool                 DatafnExecutor
    18	                                          |
    19	                             DataFn auth, namespace, policy,
    20	                             hooks, rate limits, idempotency
    21	
    22	application / CLI / test / inspector
    23	   |
    24	McpFnClient capability facades and lifecycle diagnostics
    25	   |
    26	McpFnTarget: stdio | Streamable HTTP | custom
    27	   |
    28	official MCP SDK client transports and OAuth orchestration
    29	```
    30	
    31	## Runtime ownership
    32	
    33	The official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` owns initialization, JSON-RPC dispatch, stdio framing, Streamable HTTP, capability negotiation, ping, and protocol errors. McpFn does not carry a second MCP protocol implementation.
    34	
    35	`McpFnServer` owns server identity, capability derivation, request-context construction, pagination, dispatch, error normalization, client-mediated roots/sampling/elicitation, notifications, and transport connection lifecycle. One `McpFnServer` instance connects to one transport. A host accepting multiple connections creates one server instance per connection while sharing the immutable registry.
    36	
    37	`McpFnRegistry` owns the application contract. It registers tools, exact resources, URI-template resources, prompts, completions, subscriptions, and task-capable tool handlers. Ajv validates tool and prompt inputs. URI templates are parsed once at registration. Task-capable tools require an explicit SDK `TaskStore`. MCP App links are validated across the full registry before a server or manifest is created.
    38	
    39	`McpFnServerDeclaration` is the side-effect-free application facade. It owns a
    40	registry, identity, transports, extensions, and client requirements; the same
    41	declaration creates manifests and per-connection server runtimes. Existing
    42	`McpFnServer` construction remains supported.
    43	
    44	## Client and session ownership
    45	
    46	`@mcpfn/client` owns target description, connection state, initialization,
    47	complete inventory pagination, tool/resource/prompt/task facades, explicit
    48	authorization callback completion, explicit reconnection, and bounded redacted
    49	diagnostics. It uses official SDK transports and protocol objects. It may retry
    50	connection establishment when configured; it never replays a caller's tool or
    51	other capability operation.
    52	
    53	The testing package wraps this production client for in-memory and external
    54	targets. The inspector records its diagnostics and invokes its facades. The CLI
    55	constructs its stdio or HTTP targets. This one-way dependency rule prevents
    56	test-only, inspector-only, or command-line protocol forks.
    57	
    58	## Authorization ownership
    59	
    60	The official SDK owns RFC discovery, DCR, PKCE construction, token exchange,
    61	refresh, and transport challenge handling. `@mcpfn/auth` supplies secure state
    62	and integration policy:
    63	
    64	- exact redirect matching with only the RFC 8252 loopback-port exception;
    65	- callback-state correlation before token exchange;
    66	- memory-only credentials by default or application-supplied encrypted storage;
    67	- redacted, bounded diagnostics and read-only discovery probes;
    68	- protected-resource verification and conversion to trusted SDK `authInfo`;
    69	- hosted metadata, registration, and authorization-request compatibility while
    70	  login, consent, signing, token issuance, and durable identity stay with the
    71	  host application.
    72	
    73	Client ID Metadata Document fetching is HTTPS-only, size-bounded, and requires
    74	an application allow-policy before any external URL is fetched. Additional
    75	advertised grant types do not invalidate a client that supports the requested
    76	authorization-code flow.
    77	
    78	## Manifest compatibility
    79	
    80	`createManifest` emits code-unit-sorted tool, resource, template, and prompt inventories plus a SHA-256 hash over a canonically ordered JSON representation. Object-valued capabilities, client requirements, and extensions retain their supplied insertion order in the returned body; their order does not affect the hash. `diffManifests` classifies changes as:
    81	
    82	- `breaking`: removed tools/properties/support, narrowed input enums, widened output enums, tighter input constraints, relaxed output constraints, newly required inputs, required output additions, and any output property added to a previously closed schema;
    83	- `additive`: added tools, optional input properties, optional output properties accepted by a previously open schema, widened input enums, relaxed input constraints, and added protocol/transport support;
    84	- `behavioral`: titles, descriptions, or annotations that can alter model tool selection without changing JSON validity.
    85	
    86	The diff is deliberately structural. Semantic scenarios are still required for authorization decisions, version resolution, idempotency, side effects, error envelopes, and result meaning.
    87	
    88	## DataFn integration
    89	
    90	`DatafnServer.executor` is an in-process boundary over the same query, mutation, transaction, and search handlers used by HTTP. It preserves authorization callbacks, namespace and actor derivation, schema permissions, plugins, rate limits, payload limits, and DataFn error envelopes.
    91	
    92	`@mcpfn/datafn` consumes that executor. It never accepts tenant, principal, namespace, or DataFn `clientId` values as tool arguments. Reads default on only after a resource is explicitly exposed; writes never default on.
    93	
    94	## Security invariants
    95	
    96	- Treat names, descriptions, annotations, schemas, and output shapes as versioned public contracts.
    97	- Build trusted context from the transport/authentication layer, not model-provided arguments.
    98	- Keep `additionalProperties: false` unless unknown keys are an intentional contract.
    99	- Prefer explicit output schemas for stable consumers.
   100	- Mark destructive and read-only annotations accurately; they influence client UX but do not replace server authorization.
   101	- Do not expose DataFn fields that its resolved read/write capabilities reject.
   102	- Require OAuth resource indicators and scopes at the HTTP boundary; never infer identity from model arguments.
   103	- Treat MCP Apps as untrusted HTML and declare the narrowest CSP and permissions.
   104	- Never write authorization codes, states, verifiers, tokens, cookies, or URL
   105	  credentials to diagnostic, inspection, or test artifacts.

     2	
     3	A regression-free MCP project needs five independent layers.
     4	
     5	| Layer | What it catches | McpFn surface |
     6	| --- | --- | --- |
     7	| Unit/domain | Handler logic, authorization, persistence, policy | Existing package tests |

    10	| Authentication | API keys, OAuth challenges, scopes, audience, expiry, revocation, PKCE, refresh, and client metadata | `@mcpfn/testing/auth` and `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` |
    11	| Protocol conformance | Initialization, JSON-RPC, transport, and MCP specification behavior | Official `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance` via `mcpfn conformance` |

    13	## Contract baseline
    14	
    15	Generate a candidate manifest from a module whose default export is a `McpFnServer`, an async factory returning one, a `McpFnRegistry`, or an existing manifest:
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	mcpfn manifest ./mcp-server.ts --output ./candidate.manifest.json
    19	mcpfn diff ./mcpfn.manifest.json ./candidate.manifest.json --fail-on-behavioral
    20	```
    21	
    22	For a registry export, pass both `--name` and `--version`. Exit code `1` means the diff found a breaking change, or a behavioral change when requested. Exit code `2` means the source or command was invalid.
    23	
    24	Review additive changes before replacing the committed baseline. A compatible diff means old inputs remain structurally accepted; it does not prove the new tool is authorized or semantically correct.

    26	## Semantic scenarios
    27	
    28	```ts
    29	import type { McpFnScenario } from "@mcpfn/testing";
    30	
    31	export default [
    32	  {
    33	    name: "resolves the published version",
    34	    tool: "skill_get",
    35	    arguments: { slug: "work-linear-issue" },
    36	    expect: {
    37	      isError: false,
    38	      structuredContent: {
    39	        skill: { slug: "work-linear-issue", version: 3 },
    40	      },
    41	      structuredTextParity: true,
    42	    },
    43	  },
    44	] satisfies McpFnScenario[];
    45	```
    46	
    47	`mcpfn test` connects the production McpFn client and server with the official
    48	in-memory transport. `mcpfn test-target` runs the same scenarios against stdio
    49	or Streamable HTTP. Both check or exercise the real capability boundary.
    50	`McpFnTestClient` also exposes resources, prompts, completions, subscriptions,
    51	and experimental task APIs; its `configure` hook installs client-side roots,
    52	sampling, elicitation, and notification handlers before initialization.
    53	
    54	`structuredTextParity` is appropriate only when the text block is JSON representing the same object as `structuredContent`. Human-readable text such as MemoryFn's search summary should be asserted separately.

    56	For tools with a declared success `outputSchema`, assert error codes by parsing the JSON text block: McpFn intentionally omits structured error content so it cannot be rejected against the success schema.

    58	## Authentication
    59	
    60	`assertAuthRegressionSuite()` runs the transport-level API-key or OAuth matrix against a caller-provided protected operation. The thin provider adapter maps credential issuance and revocation to the application's existing test support.     61	
    62	The `@mcpfn/testing/playwright` subpath exports a Playwright `test` extended with `mcpfnOAuth`.     61	refresh, and transport challenge handling. `@mcpfn/auth` supplies secure state
    62	and integration policy:

    64	- exact redirect matching with only the RFC 8252 loopback-port exception;

The browser flow is a single generic, internally consistent mock and never passes through the production McpFn client authorization lifecycle.

+Per-requirement defect notes:
+
+### Release and package selection (`MCP2-AC-01`, `MCP2-AC-16`)
+
+`@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/inspector` are runtime dependencies of other publishable packages but are absent from `release-packages.json`. `scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs` loads only that file and rejects unlisted slugs. This is outside `gate:mcpfn-release`, so both local and CI gates pass. Live `npm view` returned E404 for both packages at `0.0.1`; therefore workspace and temporary-tarball proof must not be described as current published-package availability.
+
+### Authorization boundary (`MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-10`)
+
+The generic provider seam authenticates but does not invoke `AuthProvider.authorize`, even though the shared auth middleware treats that method as the resource authorization boundary. Its local `options.authorize` callback is not a substitute because existing AuthProvider policy is silently discarded. The adapter also accepts requests with no bearer header if `authenticate` returns a session, sets an empty SDK token, spreads arbitrary `principal.extra` after authoritative keys, and omits the RFC bearer challenge on rejection.
+
+The hosted authorization handler is a useful authorization-request validator, but it is not the complete fixed role-3 adapter described by the issue. It unconditionally advertises `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and `none`/`client_secret_basic`/`client_secret_post`, yet the `token(request)` callback contract exposes no capability declaration from which those values could be derived or validated. State is optional; raw token/revoke parsing and all post-authorization lifecycle behavior remain outside McpFn.
+
+### OAuth metadata fetch (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`)
+
+Client ID Metadata Documents are allow-checked once, then fetched with default redirect behavior and no deadline. A permitted public HTTPS URL can redirect to a disallowed/private or non-HTTPS target unless a custom fetch prevents it. Both request registration bodies and metadata responses are converted with `text()` before the byte cap is enforced, so content-length omission/chunking defeats the allocation bound.
+
+### Lifecycle and diagnostics (`MCP2-AC-03`, `MCP2-AC-04`)
+
+`McpFnTargetContext` includes an optional signal, but `connectInternal` supplies no signal and `close()` does not coordinate with `connectPromise`. `configure` executes after target/protocol allocation but outside the connect cleanup block. Unexpected `protocol.onclose` changes only state and leaves stale references. Diagnostic sinks are awaited as part of core control flow, so a consumer observer can abort connect/close/auth and convert successful capability execution into apparent failure.
+
+### Reports and redaction (`MCP2-AC-04`, `MCP2-AC-13`, `MCP2-AC-15`)
+
+The key regex's unanchored `authorization` alternative treats public discovery field names as secrets. The URL query regex does not cover `api_key`, `password`, `cookie`, or generic credential names and never redacts fragments. `runScenarios` records raw exception messages. `runMcpFnTargetSuite` copies raw custom target descriptors. Inspector events and snapshots have no count or byte cap. These behaviors violate both secrecy and diagnostic usefulness.
+
+### OAuth proof (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-08`)
+
+The Playwright flow proves an internally consistent local mock can approve, exchange, refresh/rotate, and revoke. It does not use the named fixtures or production `McpFnClient.completeAuthorization` path. The ChatGPT/Claude tests call `/authorize` and receive application JSON; they do not generate a code or call `/token`. No test covers state replay, production callback failure cleanup, refresh serialization, token-auth method negotiation, expiry/denial in the browser lane, or named invalid metadata beyond a redirect mismatch.
+
+### Inspector/scenario contract (`MCP2-AC-15`)
+
+`McpFnInspector.exportScenario` returns `{name, operation: {kind, name, arguments}, expect}`. `runScenarios` expects `{name, kind, tool|uri|prompt, arguments, expect}`. The mismatch is structural and reproduced directly. Even after flattening, an inspector `CallToolResult` cannot be assigned wholesale to the runner's narrow tool expectation without an explicit conversion contract.
+
+### Server declaration (`MCP2-AC-02`)
+
+The declaration says it is side-effect-free but mutates a caller-supplied registry when item arrays are also provided. Its `manifest()` uses declaration-time capabilities, while `createServer(runtime)` can add `additionalCapabilities` and task-store flags. A probe produced `{}` from the declaration manifest and `{logging:{}}` from the runtime manifest for the same declaration, undermining the same-declaration release/test guarantee.

It unconditionally advertises `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and `none`/`client_secret_basic`/`client_secret_post`, yet the `token(request)` callback contract exposes no capability declaration from which those values could be derived or validated. State is optional; raw token/revoke parsing and all post-authorization lifecycle behavior remain outside McpFn.

### OAuth metadata fetch (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`)

Client ID Metadata Documents are allow-checked once, then fetched with default redirect behavior and no deadline. A permitted public HTTPS URL can redirect to a disallowed/private or non-HTTPS target unless a custom fetch prevents it. Both request registration bodies and metadata responses are converted with `text()` before the byte cap is enforced, so content-length omission/chunking defeats the allocation bound.

### Lifecycle and diagnostics (`MCP2-AC-03`, `MCP2-AC-04`)

`McpFnTargetContext` includes an optional signal, but `connectInternal` supplies no signal and `close()` does not coordinate with `connectPromise`. `configure` executes after target/protocol allocation but outside the connect cleanup block. Unexpected `protocol.onclose` changes only state and leaves stale references. Diagnostic sinks are awaited as part of core control flow, so a consumer observer can abort connect/close/auth and convert successful capability execution into apparent failure.

### Reports and redaction (`MCP2-AC-04`, `MCP2-AC-13`, `MCP2-AC-15`)

The key regex's unanchored `authorization` alternative treats public discovery field names as secrets. The URL query regex does not cover `api_key`, `password`, `cookie`, or generic credential names and never redacts fragments. `runScenarios` records raw exception messages. `runMcpFnTargetSuite` copies raw custom target descriptors. Inspector events and snapshots have no count or byte cap. These behaviors violate both secrecy and diagnostic usefulness.

### OAuth proof (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-08`)

The Playwright flow proves an internally consistent local mock can approve, exchange, refresh/rotate, and revoke. It does not use the named fixtures or production `McpFnClient.completeAuthorization` path. The ChatGPT/Claude tests call `/authorize` and receive application JSON; they do not generate a code or call `/token`. No test covers state replay, production callback failure cleanup, refresh serialization, token-auth method negotiation, expiry/denial in the browser lane, or named invalid metadata beyond a redirect mismatch.

### Inspector/scenario contract (`MCP2-AC-15`)

`McpFnInspector.exportScenario` returns `{name, operation: {kind, name, arguments}, expect}`. `runScenarios` expects `{name, kind, tool|uri|prompt, arguments, expect}`. The mismatch is structural and reproduced directly. Even after flattening, an inspector `CallToolResult` cannot be assigned wholesale to the runner's narrow tool expectation without an explicit conversion contract.

### Server declaration (`MCP2-AC-02`)

The declaration says it is side-effect-free but mutates a caller-supplied registry when item arrays are also provided. Its `manifest()` uses declaration-time capabilities, while `createServer(runtime)` can add `additionalCapabilities` and task-store flags. A probe produced `{}` from the declaration manifest and `{logging:{}}` from the runtime manifest for the same declaration, undermining the same-declaration release/test guarantee.

## Spec conflicts / spec gaps (explicit)

No direct contradictory requirement was found between the live issue and its documents. The architecture statement that phases need not land atomically is a sequencing allowance, not a relaxation of the issue's final acceptance criteria. Because no phase or reduced scope was selected, incomplete later phases remain compliance failures for this full audit.

Gaps:

1. **SPEC MISSING:** no formal requirement IDs or referenced test-vector files. This report assigned IDs but cannot map to a versioned requirements artifact.
2. **SPEC MISSING:** the approved first-release runtime matrix is unresolved. Package engines imply Node 18.18+, conformance uses Node 22, but browser/edge/desktop/native support and subpath portability are not decided.
3. **SPEC MISSING:** no versioning/compatibility policy for diagnostic events, scenario JSON, artifacts, stored credentials, or inspector exports.
4. **SPEC MISSING:** no versioned scenario schema or artifact schema, despite acceptance requiring machine-readable stability.
5. **SPEC MISSING:** no approved AuthFn adapter placement. The implementation puts it in the base package and adds a hard runtime dependency, contrary to the architecture's recommended optional/peer direction.
6. **SPEC MISSING:** no governance/version/provenance contract for named host fixtures or scheduled drift checks.
7. **SPEC MISSING:** no exact named consumer selected for the mandatory release gate; docs explicitly exclude LangFn, MemoryFn, ProbeFn, and downstream Skillplane.
8. **SPEC MISSING:** the hosted token-authority adapter capability contract does not define how supported grants/token-auth methods/refresh/revocation are declared, although metadata must be accurate.

## Cross-cutting audits (security/determinism/limits/errors/compat)

### Security/authz/validation boundaries

- FAIL: AuthProvider resource authorization is bypassed.
- FAIL: trusted `AuthInfo.extra` fields can be overwritten by mapped extras.
- FAIL: generic provider 401s omit the protected-resource bearer challenge.
- FAIL: metadata fetch redirect targets are not re-authorized and have no timeout.
- FAIL: secret redaction misses query/hash values and raw scenario/report errors.
- PARTIAL: resource-server bearer validation, expiry, resource equality, and scope enforcement remain strong in the existing dedicated handler.
- PARTIAL: exact redirect validation is strong for implemented web/loopback cases, but the complete native/host/metadata matrix is absent.
- PARTIAL: memory-only default and cipher-based storage exist, but stale single-use verifier data is not cleared after exchange and refresh concurrency is unproven.

### Determinism invariants

- PASS: redirect mismatch and loopback-port behavior are deterministic and fail before browser open.
- PASS: local stdio and HTTP round trips, manifest diff, scenarios, and official conformance are deterministic in the current gate.
- FAIL: close-vs-connect, configure failure, and observer failure are not deterministic lifecycle-safe contracts.
- FAIL: named host fixtures are constant-shape checks rather than independent deterministic flows.
- PARTIAL: target/session unification is correct, but scenario/task/notification coverage is incomplete.

### Limits/caps

- PASS: auth discovery requests have a configurable timeout.
- PASS: the shared redactor caps depth, array entries, and string length for values it processes.
- FAIL: hosted metadata fetch has no timeout and buffers before enforcing max bytes.
- FAIL: inspector event retention is unbounded and every snapshot/timeline copies the full history.
- FAIL: suite reports and raw error strings have no aggregate byte/count cap.
- FAIL: scenario operations have no shared timeout/cancellation contract.

### Error handling + canonical envelopes

- PASS: `McpFnClientError` carries code, phase, and retryability for some lifecycle failures.
- FAIL: observer failures escape as operation/lifecycle errors.
- FAIL: `configure` failures bypass cleanup and canonical wrapping.
- FAIL: `test-target` connection/auth/runtime failures use exit 2, conflating execution failures with invalid configuration.
- FAIL: hosted auth converts malformed resource URLs and many adapter failures into generic `server_error`; token/revoke errors are wholly consumer-defined.
- FAIL: authorization-browser open and no-op revocation diagnostics can report success inaccurately; verifier cleanup outcome is absent.
- PARTIAL: resource-server errors use stable OAuth envelopes and challenges.

### Compatibility/versioning/migrations

- PASS: current server/test APIs remain and new facades layer on them.
- PASS: ESM/CJS workspace and temporary packed imports pass on Node 22; CJS import also passed on local Node 20.
- FAIL: new package release slugs are absent; published availability is not proven.
- FAIL: declaration and runtime manifests can differ.
- FAIL: inspector export is not compatible with the scenario runner.
- PARTIAL: docs inventory LangFn/Skillplane overlap, but no parity/single-writer migration proof exists.
- PARTIAL: the base auth package forces an AuthFn runtime dependency despite AuthFn being an optional integration.
- PARTIAL: no pre-1.0 schema/version policy exists for reports, credentials, diagnostics, or exports.

## Recommendations (ranked)

1. **Block merge/release and repair the trusted authorization seam** (`Intent 8, 22, 27, 28`; `MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-10`). Invoke provider resource authorization or define one authoritative capability-aware decision contract, fail closed, prevent extra-field overrides, require/handle credentials deliberately, and emit the same bearer challenge as the resource-server handler. Add denial/missing-token/resource tests.
2. **Make the hosted role-3 contract real or narrow its claims** (`Intent 16–27`; `MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-08`). Define adapter capabilities, derive metadata, centralize token/grant/auth-method validation and error mapping, require state/resource policy, and add independent ChatGPT/Claude code+PKCE+token+MCP flows plus incompatible cases.
3. **Harden Client ID Metadata Document I/O** (`Intent 17, 27`; `MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`). Disable automatic redirects or revalidate every hop, enforce HTTPS/address policy on each hop, add an abort deadline, stream with a byte counter, and cap decompressed bytes. Add redirect-to-private, slow, and chunked oversized vectors.
4. **Fix lifecycle ownership before calling the client lifecycle-safe** (`Intent 10–11`; `MCP2-AC-03`, `MCP2-AC-04`). Use a generation/abort controller for connect attempts, pass `signal` to targets, await/cancel pending opens on close, close late handles, wrap configure in cleanup/retry logic, clear stale protocol/handle state on unexpected close, and isolate diagnostic observers.
5. **Replace the redaction matcher with explicit normalized secret keys and URL handling** (`Intent 14, 37–41`; `MCP2-AC-04`, `MCP2-AC-13`, `MCP2-AC-15`). Preserve public authorization metadata, redact credentials/query/fragment comprehensively, sanitize error strings and target descriptors at the report boundary, and add negative leakage tests.
6. **Complete release registration and strengthen the installed-package gate** (`Intent 42–43`; `MCP2-AC-16`). Add client/inspector release entries, validate release tag resolution, pack/install all seven packages including DataFn, run representative stdio/HTTP client/server behavior from tarballs, execute the production client example, and name an in-scope parity consumer or explicitly revise the criterion.
7. **Define one versioned scenario/artifact contract and make inspector export use it** (`Intent 32, 37–41`; `MCP2-AC-13`, `MCP2-AC-15`). Include task/notification/auth expectations, timeouts/cancellation, side-effect metadata, redacted variables, incomplete status, size caps, and stable exit taxonomy. Add round-trip inspector-export → CLI/test coverage.
8. **Close the OAuth test matrix** (`Intent 20–26, 33–34`; `MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-08`). Add state replay, issuer/resource, native/IPv6/localhost, multiple redirects, independent DCR/CIMD drift, token auth negotiation, denial/expiry, refresh concurrency, unsupported grants, stale registration, and production client callback cleanup.
9. **Restore same-declaration invariants** (`Intent 6–7`; `MCP2-AC-02`). Avoid mutating supplied registries and compute declaration/runtime manifests from the same effective capabilities, including task-store and runtime additions. Add exact parity tests.
10. **Resolve Phase 0 specification gaps** (`Intent 5, 29, 38, 46`; `MCP2-AC-01`, `MCP2-AC-09`, `MCP2-AC-11`, `MCP2-AC-13`). Commit an ADR/runtime matrix, optional AuthFn dependency direction, shared OAuth reuse inventory, and versioning policies before stabilizing any 0.x public formats.

content.text:
Audit complete: MCP-2 is **not merge-ready or release-ready**. Coverage is **5 PASS, 6 PARTIAL, 6 FAIL** across the 17 acceptance criteria.

Key findings:

- [release-packages.json](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/release-packages.json:57) omits the new `@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/inspector` packages, so the normal release workflow cannot select them. Both return npm E404 at `0.0.1`.
- [provider-adapter.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/auth/src/provider-adapter.ts:43) authenticates but never calls `AuthProvider.authorize()`. A deny-all probe was accepted with zero authorization calls.
- [hosted-authorization.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/auth/src/hosted-authorization.ts:292) delegates raw token/revoke behavior while advertising hard-coded grants and authentication methods. The required hosted role-3 ownership is incomplete.
- Metadata-document fetching checks only the initial URL, follows redirects without revalidation or timeout, and buffers the entire body before enforcing its size limit.
- [client.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/client/src/client.ts:169) can become connected after `close()` completes. Configure and unexpected-close paths can also leak state.
- Diagnostic listener failures propagate into client operations. A successful state-changing tool call executed once but rejected with the observer’s error.
- [redaction.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/packages/oauth-core/src/redaction.ts:3) hides useful authorization metadata while leaking `api_key`, `password`, and fragment credentials.
- ChatGPT/Claude tests validate request shapes, not independent authorization-code + PKCE end-to-end flows.
- [inspector export](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/inspector/src/index.ts:99) produces a shape rejected by the shared scenario runner.
- The release gate does not execute the production client example—which calls nonexistent `calculator_add`—or perform a representative round trip using installed tarballs.

Verification:

- All 112 focused affected-package tests passed.
- The full local Node 22 `gate:mcpfn-release` passed, matching exact-head CI.
- PR #122 remains `UNSTABLE`: the generic JavaScript failure is in UIFn, while SonarCloud separately fails its new-code reliability gate.
- Only the required audit report and append-only audit log were changed.
